# streamtime_package (Resource)

A chart or image version in the package catalog, with how Streamtime treats it. Managing the catalog needs the catalog permission, normally held by the root organization.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "streamtime_package" "kafka" {
  registry_url   = "https://charts.example.com"
  repository     = "kafka"
  tag            = "31.0.0"
  support_status = "supported"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `registry_url` (String) The registry or chart repository address. Changing it creates a new package.
- `repository` (String) The repository name. Changing it creates a new package.
- `tag` (String) The version tag. Changing it creates a new package.

### Optional

- `artifact_type` (String) What the package is: container_image, helm_chart or oci_artifact.
- `default_values` (String) The package's default chart values, set with jsonencode({...}).
- `preferred_registry` (String) The registry to pull the package from when more than one holds it.
- `support_notes` (String) Notes for people choosing a version.
- `support_status` (String) How Streamtime treats the version: active, supported, deprecated, latest or preview.
- `template_values` (String) Chart values applied for this package, set with jsonencode({...}).
- `values_schema` (String) A JSON schema for the chart values, set with jsonencode({...}).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the package. Use it to import an existing one.
- `identifier` (String) The package ID Streamtime assigns. Use it to import an existing package.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the package ID.
terraform import streamtime_package.kafka kafka-31.0.0
```
